kurz: Sear the meat, then cook it gently, covered, in a little liquid for hours. The connective tissue turns into gelatine and the meat turns tender.
bild_im_kopf: Like a long bath instead of a hot shower: the warmth has time to reach everywhere and loosen everything.
was_passiert: Searing brings roasted aromas into the meat and the pan residue. In the gently simmering liquid, the [[kollagen-gelatine|collagen]] dissolves into gelatine over hours. If the liquid boils hard, the muscle fibres squeeze out too much juice and the meat turns dry and stringy.
warum_wichtig: Turns cheap, tough cuts into the most tender dishes of all.
faustregeln: Braises often taste better the next day: gelatine and aromas settle.
schritte: Pat the meat dry and sear it hard in batches.
Brown the vegetables, deglaze the pan residue with wine or stock.
Return the meat, liquid to about halfway up.
Cover and simmer gently over low heat or in the oven at 140–150 °C.
Check after 2–3 hours: a fork should slide in without resistance.
